To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mechanical properties of β Ti-alloy can be tailored by controlling the heat treatment conditions and that the in situ formed TiB precipitates can improve the strength of the β Ti-alloys without compromising the ductility and biocompatibility.
the presence of TiB precipitations in the matrix increases strength and elastic modulus of the alloy but reduces ductility and cell spreading.

the presence of ω and α phases in the matrix of TNZT and TNZTB alloys respectively, has greater effect on strength than the presence of TiB precipitate in the matrix of boron containing alloy, the elastic modulus of both the alloys is independent of the heat treatment conditions, and the cell attachment of both the alloys are superior than the control material.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of in situ reinforcements on the mechanical properties and biocorrosion behavior of β Ti-alloy and also the role of heat treatment.
the effect of heat treatment conditions on the mechanical properties and biocorrosion resistance of β Ti-alloy.
the development of a new β Ti-alloy (TNZTB), which has higher strength than the boron free TNZT alloy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of TiB particles in Ti-alloy matrix improves the mechanical properties and biocorrosion resistance, but reduces the cell adhesion and biocompatibility.
the TNZTB alloys with ω phase in the α matrix offer the highest hardness and strength, whereas the TNZT alloys with α matrix offer better biocompatibility than the boron free TNZTB alloys.
the heat treatment conditions have a significant effect on mechanical properties and cell response of the TNZ alloys.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TNZTB alloys are suitable for biomedical applications as they show higher strength and hardness and better corrosion resistance than the TNZTB samples.
the presence of ω precipitates in the β matrix increases the strength but decreases the ductility of the TNZ alloys.
the presence of in situ formed TiB particles in a β Ti matrix improves the mechanical properties, but decreases the biocompatibility of the alloy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of ω precipitates in the TNZTB matrix is not detrimental to the mechanical properties of the alloy and it is a good candidate for biomedical application.

the presence of ω and TiB precipitates enhances the strength and elastic modulus of the Ti-alloys, while the α and TiB precipitations do not show a significant influence on the strength and elastic property of the Ti-alloy.
the TNZT and TNZTB alloy samples containing β phase show higher strength and hardness than those containing α phase.
